defects: Heavy moiré and aliasing on the guilloché dial pattern at 100%. It shimmers and crawls rather than reading as engraved metal, and it is worst in the dark blue macro shot and the wide brown shots.

The dial wordmark 'ATELIER VAUCLAIR' and 'CALIBRE 9' are broken. Letterforms are fragmented, the spacing is uneven and the text dissolves into the pattern, so it reads like an aliased texture rather than printed or engraved type.
The window-shadow gobo is too soft and too uniform. It lies on the dial like a flat multiply layer, with no proper occlusion or contact against the indices and hands.
Hands and indices look CG-clean, with no bevel highlights or polish falloff. The case edges have a plastic specular rim and no real metal reflection.
Dead air of about 1 s around second 8 (change 1.3/s): a near-static frame before the end card with no motivating beat.
The blue macro shot is underlit and muddy, with crushed blacks, a low-contrast pattern and visible banding in the gradient falloff.
End-card type ('Monday.' / '150 pieces.') is a generic Didone set with no hierarchy tension. The small line is undersized and sits awkwardly against the watch.
gaps: Motion is a sequence of slow push-ins and light sweeps of the same weight. There is no escalation, no mechanical event (crown, movement or hand snap) used as a peak, and no shot that hands off to the next through a match cut, so the Friday-to-Monday time passage is told with captions instead of choreography.

Finish is far below luxury-watch standard. The guilloché needs proper texture filtering and supersampling, real anisotropic metal with environment reflections, and crisp, legible dial printing; at 100% the image currently reads as shimmering procedural noise.

The sound is sectional but simple: tick clicks over sustained, fairly static tonal pads with block cuts at about 2.4, 4.9, 7.3 and 9.7 s. There is no designed foley layer (escapement, crown, metal, room), and there is no dynamic build to a climax, just level plateaus and a hard drop, so the score doesn't carry the time-passing idea.
